results.title: Attention Is All You Need - Wikipedia
results.content:
"Attention Is All You Need" is a 2017 research paper on machine learning authored by eight scientists and engineers working at Google. The paper introduced a new deep learning architecture known as the transformer "Transformer (deep learning)"), based on the attention mechanism "Attention (machine learning)") proposed in 2014 by Bahdanau et al. The transformer approach it describes has become the main architecture of a wide variety of artificial intelligence systems, including large language [...] [edit]

The authors of the paper are Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan Gomez, Łukasz Kaiser"), and Illia Polosukhin. All eight authors were "equal contributors" to the paper; the listed order was randomized (according to the paper itself). After the paper, each of the authors left Google to join other companies or to found startups. [...] As of 2026,( the paper has been cited more than 250,000 times, placing it among the top ten most-cited papers of the 21st century. After the paper was published by Google, each of the eight authors left the company to join other companies or to found startups.

 mechanism. It hit me that I really need to introduce the first author of the foundational paper _Attention is All You Need_, Ashish Vaswani. So, the star of my seventeenth piece is none other than Ashish Vaswani.

## About Ashish [...] Ashish was born in 1986 in India. He’s the kind of scholar who skyrocketed to fame because of a single paper. But before that game-changing attention paper, his research during his PhD was already focused on natural language processing. His PhD advisors were Liang Huang and David Chiang. His most notable PhD work? A paper where he was the first author, with Liang Huang and David Chiang as co-authors, called _Smaller Alignment Models for Better Translations: Unsupervised Word Alignment with the [...] Alignment with the ℓ0-norm_. This paper improved unsupervised word alignment models, boosting the accuracy of alignment and the quality of machine translations. Fun fact: a lot of breakthroughs in language models are tied to machine translation. Even _Attention is All You Need_ used English-to-German sequence-to-sequence translation data for training. results.title: USC Alumni Paved Path for ChatGPT | Information Sciences Institute
results.content:
ChatGPT has taken the world by storm, but seeds of the groundbreaking technology were sown at the USC Viterbi School of Engineering. The seminal paper “Attention Is All You Need,” which laid the foundation for ChatGPT and other generative AI systems, was co-authored by Ashish Vaswani, a PhD computer science graduate (’14) and Niki Parmar, a master’s in computer science graduate (’15). [...] As of publishing, “Attention Is All You Need” has received more than 60,000 citations, according to Google Scholar. Its total citation count continues to increase as researchers build on its insights and apply transformer architecture techniques to new problems, from image and music generation, to predicting protein properties for medicine. [...] The landmark paper was presented at the 2017 Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS), one of the top conferences in AI and machine learning. In the paper, the researchers introduced the transformer architecture, a powerful type of neural network that has become widely used for natural language processing tasks, from text classification to language modeling.

##### Attention is all you need

The paper, published at NeurIPS in 2017, has been cited more than 60,000 times.

results.title: AI Research Recap: Ok Transformers, You have My Attention
results.content:
In 2017, Ashish Vaswani (and 7 other Google Researchers) published a research paper at the 31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems titled very simply “Attention Is All You Need”. Despite this quaint title, their 15 page paper described a new architecture for language models that revolutionized the state of the art at that time and kickstarted the future of AI leading to the GPT based large language models that we have today. Since its publication “Attention Is All You Need” has [...] This brings us to a chief insight of the “Attention is All You Need” paper. How can we build a neural network that can understand sentence structure across large pieces of text, without needing to go through them one-by-one? Turns out you can using a new simple neural network architecture they call a “Transformer”.

“AutoBots rollout … self-attention layers with positional embeddings for scalable neural network training!” [...] All You Need” has been cited in over 120,000 other works. I recently sat down with this paper (assisted heavily by the paper’s great-great grandchild ChatGPT) and tried to understand what made it so revolutionary.
